Zero-inflated negative binomial regression

Source: R/zinbreg.R
zinbreg.Rd

Fits a zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) model. With probability \(\pi_i\) observation \(i\) is a structural zero; otherwise it comes from an NB2 distribution with mean \(\mu_i\) and dispersion \(\theta\). The count model is \(\log\mu_i = x_i^\top\beta + o_i\) and the zero-inflation model is \(\mathrm{logit}\,\pi_i = z_i^\top\gamma\).

Usage

zinbreg(formula, data, offset, control = zinbreg_control())

Arguments

formula

A two-part formula y ~ x1 + x2 | z1 + z2: count-model covariates before |, zero-model covariates after it. Without |, the same covariates are used in both parts. An offset() term is allowed in the count part only.

data

A data frame containing the variables in formula.

offset

An optional offset for the count model (e.g. log exposure), evaluated in data.

control

A list of settings from zinbreg_control().

Value

An object of class "zinbreg", a list with components

coefficients

a list with elements count (\(\hat\beta\)) and zero (\(\hat\gamma\))

vcov

variance-covariance matrix of \((\hat\beta, \hat\gamma)\); names are prefixed count_ and zero_

theta, SE.theta, SE.logtheta

estimated dispersion parameter and the standard errors of \(\hat\theta\) and \(\log\hat\theta\)

vcov_full

variance-covariance matrix of \((\hat\beta, \hat\gamma, \log\hat\theta)\)

loglik, loglik_path

maximized log-likelihood and its value at every EM iteration

iter, converged

number of EM iterations and convergence flag

fitted.values

\((1 - \hat\pi_i)\hat\mu_i\), the fitted mean of \(Y_i\)

mu, pi, tau

fitted count means, structural-zero probabilities, and final E-step posterior probabilities

y, offset, nobs, df.residual

response, offset, number of observations, and residual degrees of freedom

call, formula, terms, model, xlevels, contrasts, control

information used to print the fit and to predict for new data

Details

The model is fitted by the EM algorithm. The E-step computes the posterior probability \(\tau_i\) that each zero is a structural zero. The M-step fits (i) a logistic regression of \(\tau_i\) on \(z_i\) by IRLS and (ii) a weighted NB regression with prior weights \(1 - \tau_i\) by the same IRLS / Newton-Raphson algorithm as nbreg(). Iterations stop when the observed-data log-likelihood changes by less than control$epsilon. No general-purpose numerical maximizer is used.

EM does not produce standard errors. They are obtained by inverting the negative Hessian of the observed-data log-likelihood with respect to \((\beta, \gamma, \log\theta)\) at the estimates. By default the Hessian is computed from analytic second derivatives; zinbreg_control(hessian = "numeric") uses numDeriv::hessian() instead.

See also

zinbreg_control(), nbreg()

Examples

# Simulated ZINB data
set.seed(1)
n <- 500
x <- rnorm(n)
z <- rnorm(n)
structural_zero <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-1 + 0.8 * z))
y <- ifelse(structural_zero == 1, 0,
            rnbinom(n, size = 2, mu = exp(1 + 0.5 * x)))
fit <- zinbreg(y ~ x | z, data = data.frame(x, z, y))
fit$coefficients
#> $count
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>   1.0953534   0.4391556 
#> 
#> $zero
#> (Intercept)           z 
#>  -1.0497237   0.8567723 
#> 
fit$theta
#> [1] 1.960634

# Publication counts of biochemistry PhD students
if (requireNamespace("pscl", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")
  fit2 <- zinbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment | ment,
                  data = bioChemists)
  fit2$coefficients
}
#> $count
#>  (Intercept)     femWomen   marMarried         kid5          phd         ment 
#>  0.404013648 -0.211906301  0.139462144 -0.167623779  0.001962561  0.024392582 
#> 
#> $zero
#> (Intercept)        ment 
#>  -0.8066567  -0.6094417 
#>
